text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch food group Nutricia's German unit Milupa withdraws baby formula Milumil in Britain amid salmonella scare. (p1)
- Dutch employers organisation VNO-NCW calls for tax cuts following Germany's decision to reduce taxes both on company profits and personal income. (p1)
- Bank unions surprised by employers' proposals for fundamental changes to current salary structure. (p1)
- Netherlands security board STE is to probe recent rise in share price of property fund Sarakreek Holding. (p1)
- Investment bank NIB and financial services group Fortis break off talks on merging their venture capital units. (p1)
- Steel concern Hoogovens says it is very close to a deal on a joint venture with struggling Belgian steel company Boel. (p3)
- Department store chain KBB reports that 1996/97 financial year ending Jan 31 will show a 40 percent drop in profits. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Liberal party (VVD) leader Frits Bolkestein moots increase in number of jobs with pay below official minimum wage. (p1)
- Surinam government lodges official complaint with Netherlands after Dutch criticised Brazil for officially receiving Surinam's former military ruler Desi Bouterse. (p1)
- Food and drink vending machines sector estimates costs of converting to Euro currency at Dfl 130 million. (p2)
- Transavia airlines president P. Legro seeks closer cooperation with KLM Royal Dutch Airlines. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Cabinet and oil companies in advanced stage of talks on cheap diesel fuel for Dutch transport sector from July 1. (p1)
- Information from video monitoring system along Amsterdam- Utrecht motorway will now be used by tax authorities and police criminal intelligence unit CRI as well. (p1)
- National labelling of beef within the European Union seems inevitable in view of recent "mad cow" (BSE) health scare. (p15)
TROUW
- City of Apeldoorn refuses to evict from their hostels asylum seekers who have been ordered to leave the country. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Interior minister Hans Dijkstal and police unions reach agreement in principle on new pay and conditions contract. (p11)
